files.summary: Complete VFS spec. It has the header block and sections 1–9: the inode and dentry model (TypeScript types and IndexedDB records, the version rule), and the standard hierarchy with owners, modes and fixed well-known UUIDv7-shaped ids (00000000-0000-7000-8000-…; directories 0x01–0x0e, synthesised files 0x100–0x103, seeded files from 0x1000 in an append-only registry). It covers mkfs and the seed-upgrade rule; /tmp as a device-local tmpfs (EXDEV across it); kernel-synthesised read-only files (/system/release and /system/log/*.log); and NFC names with byte limits (255/4096, ELOOP at the 41st hop). Path resolution is given in full pseudocode (., .., //, trailing slash, x on every component, stop one step early, EAGAIN for unmirrored directories when offline). Permissions: may() with the root x-bit fix, a permission matrix per operation, umask 022, the sticky bit, the chmod octal/symbolic grammar and evaluator, and root-only chown. Also covered: symlinks, hard links (implemented, with protected hard links and nlink rules), quotas enforced in the transaction (with df/du/quota semantics), and the open-file table with close-to-open write sessions (poisoning, so a failed write leaves no partial file). There is a syscall table with errnos for every file-system call. The mutation pipeline has two phases, in-kernel intent locks (E/N/T/G), one synchronous IndexedDB transaction, a fencing check and a wait for server confirmation of bulk ops online. Per-op rules are given for rm -r, cp -r, mv (POSIX rename matrix), batch rename, chmod/chown -R and the agent's batch (DryRun and fingerprint). The rest: the IndexedDB schema (stores, keys, indexes, durability, the migration code, blob and chunk model, GC); the undo/outbox coupling (coalescing, ack, revert cascade, parked ops); conflicts (the base each op carries, conflicted-copy naming, lost+found); local advisory locks versus server leases; remote apply, mirroring and the dcache; vfs.* events and permEpoch; the incremental trie contract; the client fault hook (abort from the onsuccess of the Nth inode-row write); fsck invariants I1–I14 with repairs; the command-to-syscall map; and what the server must mirror exactly. Also included: algorithms with complexities, errno and exception mapping, edge cases, performance budgets (every pilot number labelled), a test plan with every title starting with its requirement ID (including property tests), open questions, and cross-spec requests.

cross_spec_requests: database.md (X-DB-1): use the VFS version rule. version goes up only for content, mode/uid/gid, or a directory's entry-set change. A rename bumps only the parents; nlink, ctime and utimes never bump version. The batch-rename sketch must not bump the renamed inodes.

database.md (X-DB-2): charge quota as the VFS does. Directories cost 0 bytes, a symlink costs its target's byte length, every inode costs 1 inode, the charge goes to the owning uid, and root is exempt.

database.md (X-DB-3): seed the fixed ids in protocol/src/wellknown.ts (/, /bin, /system, /system/services, /system/log, /system/branding, /root, /home, /tmp, /mnt, plus /usr, /usr/share, /usr/share/man, /lost+found) and the seeded files from protocol/wellknown/seed-ids.json, with version = seedVersion. Apply the seed-upgrade rule (priorSha256) at deploy.

database.md (X-DB-4): compute the tree checksum and the subtree digest with the VFS §5.6 formulas (SHA-256, decimal integers, ordered by (parent, name) in byte order) instead of the md5 probe checksum.
database.md (X-DB-5): keep mode BETWEEN 0 AND 4095. Do not add CHECK (type='d' OR mode<512): the sticky bit on a file is allowed and ignored. Optionally add CHECK ((mode & 3072) = 0).
database.md (X-DB-6): no rows may exist below /tmp; an op that would create one is rejected with EXDEV. Synthesised files never exist on the server.

database.md (X-DB-7): a create whose name is already taken keeps the client's ino under the conflicted-copy name and returns keptAs. A content op whose parent is gone lands in ~/lost+found when quota allows. A content write with a stale base uses the client-supplied conflictIno.
database.md (X-DB-8): the fault trigger counts inode-row writes, the same 'node operation' unit as the client hook.

database.md (X-DB-9): re-check permissions with the isomorphic vfs/perm.ts: root's x-bit rule, the sticky rule, protected hard links, w on a directory moved to a new parent, and r+w+x on every directory for rm -r.
database.md (X-DB-10): set changed_at (ctime) with clock_timestamp() after the row lock is held, so it only increases for each inode. Remote apply relies on it for changes that do not bump version.

offline-and-sync.md (X-SYNC-1): carry the OutboxRec fields touches, awaitSync and fence, and the states reverted and parked. Implement write/utimes coalescing, the ack transaction (serverUsed* plus per-owner seqs that advance only contiguously) and the revert cascade. Define SYNC_WAIT_MS = 10 s. Add a lock.list {ino} query on the control lane and a depth-1 snapshot (GET /api/sync/snapshot?root=&depth=1) for ensureMirrored. Keep a per-owner resume set of {self, 0} ∪ owners of mirrored directories. Prefetch the logged-in user's home blobs at idle. Treat 55P03 after retries as retryable. Define the RemoteBatch and OpResult types.

offline-and-sync.md and database.md (X-SYNC-2): the affected owners of an op are the owners, before and after the op, of every inode whose row changes, plus the owners of every directory whose entry set changes.

syscall-abi.md (X-ABI-1): add the file-system calls from VFS §3.10 that are missing (fsync, access, realpath, getcwd, chdir, umask, readFile, writeFile, copy, lock.release with force, the fsck arguments) and the VfsDetail strings. stale-base, stale-plan, not-mirrored-offline and content-not-cached use EAGAIN with a detail, so no new errno is needed (no ESTALE).

syscall-abi.md (X-ABI-2): register the vfs.* topics (create, write, rename, unlink, link, chmod, chown, utimes, conflict, load, revert), their payloads and the delivery filter (r on the parent, x on every ancestor; for a rename, the side the subscriber cannot see is null).

architecture.md §4.5 / C4 store list (X-ARC-1): add the requested stores audit (security, AGT-08) and ai_files, ai_chunks, ai_vecseg, ai_lex (RAG). Note that blob_chunks is keyed by the chunk's own hash, and list the VFS indexes (by_uid_mtime, by_fs, by_ino, by_zero, by_op, by_state).

data-structures.md (X-DSA-1): dsa/tree must offer create node, add/remove/get child, a parent pointer, pre- and post-order walks, ancestors and is-ancestor. dsa/lru must offer pin/unpin and 'evict the least recently used entry that satisfies a predicate'.
data-structures.md (X-DSA-2): dsa/trie must offer removePrefix(prefix) in O(P + removed).

shell-and-terminal.md (X-SHELL-1): use the trie key scheme path:<dirIno>\0<name> with a permission check at query time (r on the directory, x on its ancestors). Also: the mv EXDEV fallback with a 'not atomic' note; ln -f and multi-source mv through batch; grep in user space (no regex in the kernel); man pages at /usr/share/man/<section>/<name>.md; and debug inject mapping rm/mv/cp to unlink/rename/copy.

boot-and-services.md (X-BOOT-1): the vfs service runs mkfs on first boot, the seed upgrade, tmpfs clearing and the synthesised-file registry, and supports a read-only recovery mount (EPERM ro-mount). svcmgr should load only manifests named /^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*\.json$/, so conflicted copies of manifests are ignored and reported in bootlog.

security-model.md (X-SEC-1): the offline guest is uid 65534 with home /tmp/guest. State the data-at-rest limit of one database per device. Own the audit store. Add protected hard links to the threat model.
memory-and-paging.md (X-MEM-1): account write-session buffers (up to 8 MiB in memory per session) and the VFS tree and dcache on the kernel line of free.
window-manager.md (X-WM-1): the File Explorer uses only the syscalls in VFS §3.22. Add the vfs.conflict notification and the Editor's 'reload / keep both' and 'locked, read-only' banners.

agentic-shell.md (X-AGT-1): consume DryRun (overwrites, deletes, chmods, chowns, touchedInodes, fingerprint), implement ConfirmVerifier.verify(pid, planHash, dryRunHash, token), handle EAGAIN stale-plan, and use keepAfterAck undo records for ai undo. Implement the grep and wc read-only tools as helper processes the kernel spawns as the uid.

rag-semantic-search.md (X-RAG-1): accepted. VfsTxnHook adds the ai_* stores to unlink transactions synchronously. Also accepted: the event payloads with inos, permEpoch (incremented on chmod, chown, rename, link, unlink and group changes), and ensureInoLoaded/pinInode for the readable set.

identity-and-branding.md (X-ID-1): accepted. /system/release and /system/log/*.log are synthesised read-only files with fixed ids (EPERM for every uid, root included). Seeded files (/system/branding/*, /system/services/*.json, /bin/*.json, man pages) get fixed registry ids.

backend-api.md (X-BE-1): provide GET /api/sync/snapshot?root=<ino>&depth=1, streaming GET /api/blobs/{sha} for lazy fetch, and a root-only fault harness that returns the same orphan probes and the §5.6 checksum.
requirements-traceability.md (X-TRACE-1): register the Plotinium IDs PVFS-01 … PVFS-18 and the invariant IDs I1–I14 used in test titles.
open_questions: Is /tmp as a device-local tmpfs (cleared at each device's boot, never synced) acceptable? The sticky-bit demo then runs on one device via su, because two browser profiles each have their own /tmp. Ask at the Week-4 defence.
Does close-to-open write semantics count as UNIX-like? Writes become visible at close or fsync, not after each write. This is what gives 'no partial data' and whole-file conflict detection.
Is returning EINVAL for rmdir .. acceptable? Linux returns ENOTEMPTY; we simplified to one errno.
Hard links are a MAY that we implement in P3. If P3 slips they move to P4; nlink is maintained correctly either way.
Is BULK_MAX_NODES = 50,000 (EINVAL too-large) acceptable if an examiner runs rm -r on a larger client subtree?
Every strict-durability figure comes from NVMe. A SATA or HDD lab machine may break the 10 ms single-op budget, so re-measure in the Week-3 client-storage spike.
Confirm the time zone for conflicted-copy dates (server default Asia/Karachi via PLOTINIUM_TZ; the device uses its configured time zone for local conflicts).
Root's edits to /system/services sync to every device through the owner-0 feed, so the BOOT-04 cycle test must run on the local stack, never on production.
Should there be a per-file size cap beyond quota and device storage? Revisit if the quota defaults in database.md exceed about 1 GiB.
